memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'But if they will confess their sins and the sins of their ancestors -
their unfaithfulness and their hostility toward me, which made me hostile
toward them so that I sent them into the land of their enemies - then when
their uncircumcised hearts are humbled and they pay for their sin, I will
remember my covenant'" - Lev 26:40-42a (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
And here comes the great turn. After all the darkness, one small word
changes everything: "But if they will confess." The whole mood of the
chapter shifts. There is a way back.

Notice what the way back is. It is not achieving, striving, or earning. It
is confession — honestly owning their sin — and a humbled heart. The
proud, hard heart that caused the ruin is finally softened, and they simply
turn back and admit the truth.

Dear reader, this is the doorway home for every one of us. We do not
return to God by cleaning ourselves up first or by presenting a record of
improvement. We return by confession — by agreeing with God about our sin
and coming with a humbled heart.

John writes the great promise: if we confess our sins, He is faithful and
just and will forgive us our sins and purify us from all unrighteousness
(1 John 1:9). David wrote that a broken and contrite heart God will not
despise (Ps 51:17).

And see what God says He will do in response: I will remember my covenant.
The whole basis of return is not the strength of their repentance but the
faithfulness of His covenant. He was bound to them by His own promise.

For us, that covenant is sealed in the blood of Christ. However far you
have gone, the way back is still confession. Come with a humbled heart. He
is faithful.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there sin I need to honestly confess rather than hide?
2. Am I trying to earn my way back to God instead of simply confessing?
3. What would coming to God with a humbled heart look like today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, I stop hiding and confess my sin honestly before You. Thank You
that the way home is a humbled heart, not an earned record. Forgive me,
and restore me. Amen.
